title: Order No. T-37885 — Transportation Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission vs. DTK Enterprises, LLC dba Midas Touch Towing.
text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 

ORDER NUMBER T-37885 

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 
VERSUS 
DTK ENTERPRISES, LLC DBA MIDAS TOUCH TOWING 

Docket No. T-37885, In re: Cancellation of Common Carrier Certificate No. 7507-A for failure 
to maintain the required insurance coverage on file with the Commission pursuant to General 
Order dated October 13, 2023. 
(Decided July 9, 2026.) 

ORDER 
Background 
The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”) issued a citation to 
DTK Enterprises, LLC dba Midas Touch Towing (“Carrier” or “Midas Touch”) dated April 6, 
2026, directing the Carrier to show cause at a hearing why its Common Carrier Certificate No. 
7507-A should not be canceled due to the Carrier’s failure to maintain the required insurance 
coverage on file with the Commission as required by the General Order dated October 13, 20231 
(“2023 General Order”). Notice of the proceeding was published in the Commission’s Official 
Bulletin dated April 10, 2026. When the hearing was convened on July 9, 2026, the Commission 
Staff appeared and presented testimonial and documentary evidence in support of its allegations. 
The Carrier did not appear at the hearing. 
Applicable Law 

The Commission’s jurisdiction over common carriers and public utilities is established by 
Article 4, Section 21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which provides in pertinent part: 
The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public 
utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law. 
It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and 
procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have 
other powers and perform other duties as provided by law. 

Louisiana statutes more specifically describe the powers of the Commission over motor carriers 
operating intrastate for hire in the transportation of persons, household goods, and waste over the 
public highways and bridges of Louisiana. The business of operating motor vehicles for hire is a 
“business affected with a public interest”;2 and, “[t]he [C]ommission has the power and authority 
necessary to supervise, govern, regulate, and control motor carriers . . . which transport household 

1 Louisiana Public Service Commission General Order dated October 13, 2023, Louisiana Public Service

as it pertains to intrastate insurance filings for motor carriers.). 
2 La. R.S. 45:161. 
Order No. T-37885

goods, passengers, or waste intrastate and to fix reasonable and just rates, fares, tolls, or charges 
for the commodities furnished or services rendered by such motor carriers.”3 Motor carriers 
include tow trucks.4 Companies engaged in the intrastate business of transporting household 
goods, passengers, or certain kinds of waste intrastate—non-hazardous oilfield wastes, non-
hazardous industrial solid wastes, and hazardous wastes—are classified as “common carriers” 
subject to the Commission’s regulation.5 The Commission shall require insurance and indemnity 
bonds, including public liability and property damage insurance, written by companies qualified 
to do business in Louisiana.6 
The 2023 General Order provides the Commission’s rules and regulations regarding 
required insurance filings for motor carriers, including that public liability and property damage 
insurance filings shall be made on a Form E, Uniform Motor Carrier Bodily Injury and Property 
Damage Liability Certificate of Insurance (“Form E”).7 The 2023 General Order specifies that 
Commission Staff may seek cancellation of a carrier’s authority after due notice and hearing upon 
a carrier’s failure to update insurance filings.8 A carrier’s certificate may be revoked after notice 
and hearing for failing to comply with applicable law or Commission order.9 Additionally, the 
Commission’s General Order dated June 7, 2006 (“2006 General Order”) authorizes the 
imposition of a $25 citation fee when a citation is issued to a Commission-jurisdictional motor 
carrier.10 
The Commission Staff’s Case 
The Commission Staff alleges that the Carrier failed to maintain proof of its bodily injury 
and property damage (“BI & PD”)11 insurance on file with the Commission in violation of the 
2023 General Order.12 Commission Staff requests that the Carrier be found guilty as alleged, that 
the Carrier’s Common Carrier Certificate No. 7507-A be canceled pursuant to La. R.S. 45:166(A), 
and that the Carrier be assessed a $25 citation fee per the 2006 General Order. In support of its 
allegations, the Commission Staff presented the testimony of Enforcement Agent Maegan Hood.

Testimony of Maegan Hood 
Agent Hood testified that she is an Enforcement Agent in the Commission’s Transportation 
Division, whose duties include receiving and reviewing insurance filings for regulated motor 
carriers. She testified further regarding her knowledge of applicable orders and statutes, including 
the requirement that regulated motor carriers file a Form E. Agent Hood stated that she is familiar 
with Midas Touch which is a towing company operating under LPSC Common Carrier Certificate 
No. 7507-A. Agent Hood attested that, on December 30, 2025, the Commission’s Transportation 
Division received a Form K13 from Prime Insurance Company indicating that the Carrier’s BI & 
PD insurance policy would be canceled effective February 3, 2026. On February 6, 2026, Agent 
Hood prepared and mailed a notice of cancellation letter to the Carrier bearing the signature of 
Transportation Administrator Tammy Burl. The letter notified the Carrier of the cancellation of its 
BI & PD insurance policy, to have its insurer submit a current Form E, to cease operations until 
the required Form E was filed, and the consequences for non-compliance. Agent Hood mailed the 
letter to the Carrier at its address on file with the Commission via United States Postal Service 
(“USPS”) regular mail. 
Agent Hood stated that the Carrier did not submit a Form E following the notice of 
cancellation. Therefore, she prepared a tentative hearing letter to the Carrier on March 13, 2026, 
regarding the Form E. The tentative hearing letter advised the Carrier that a hearing had been 
tentatively set for June 11, 2026, and if Midas Touch did not submit a Form E by March 30, 2026, 
the Commission would issue a citation. Agent Hood mailed the letter to the Carrier’s address on 
file with the Commission and emailed the letter to Midas Touch’s email address on file with the 
Commission. Attached to the tentative hearing letter was the notice of cancellation letter sent 
February 6, 2026. 
Agent Hood explained that the Commission did not receive a Form E following her mailing 
the tentative hearing letter. Consequently, she prepared, for Ms. Burl’s signature, a citation to the 
Carrier advising Midas Touch that it must appear at a hearing on June 11, 2026, that an order may 
be issued canceling its authority, and that a $25 citation fee had been assessed to its account. 
Attached to the citation were the February 6, 2026 tentative hearing letter and the March 13, 2026 
notice of cancellation. 

13 The Commission is notified of the cancellation or expiration of a carrier’s insurance through the receipt of a Form

Agent Hood testified that she mailed the citation on April 7, 2026, via USPS regular mail 
and certified mail return receipt requested to the Carrier’s address on file with the Commission. 
Agent Hood confirmed that notice of the proceeding was published in the Commission’s Official 
Bulletin dated April 10, 2026. 
Agent Hood then identified a Ruling on Joint Motion to Continue and Notice of 
Rescheduled Hearing Date issued on June 11, 2026, indicating that Midas Touch appeared when 
the matter was called on June 11, 2026, and jointly moved with Commission Staff to continue the 
hearing to July 9, 2026. 
Agent Hood advised that, as of the hearing, the Carrier did not have an updated Form E on 
file with the Commission, and Midas Touch had not filed documentation to close its LPSC 
certificate. Agent Hood stated that the Commission Staff seeks a finding that Midas Touch is guilty 
of failure to maintain required insurance filings, that Common Carrier Certificate No. 7507-A be 
canceled, and that the Carrier be required to pay the $25 citation fee.

Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law 
From the evidence presented at the hearing, we make the following findings of fact and 
conclusions of law: 
Order No. T-37885 
Page 5 
Findings of Fact 
1. The Carrier is an LPSC-regulated towing company that currently holds Common Carrier 
Certificate No. 7507-A. 
2. On December 30, 2025, the Commission received a Form K from Prime Insurance 
Company advising that the Carrier’s BI & PD insurance would be canceled effective 
February 3, 2026. 
3. On February 6, 2026, Agent Hood mailed a notice of cancellation letter via USPS 
regular mail to the Carrier at its address on file with the Commission advising that its 
BI & PD insurance had expired on February 3, 2026, providing instructions on how to 
submit replacement insurance, and instructing the Carrier to cease operations 
immediately until replacement coverage was submitted. 
4. Midas Touch did not submit a replacement Form E. On March 13, 2026, Agent Hood 
prepared a tentative hearing letter to the Carrier advising that if a replacement Form E 
was not submitted by March 30, 2026, the Commission would issue a citation, and that 
a hearing on the matter had been tentatively scheduled for June 11, 2026. She mailed 
the letter via USPS regular mail and emailed it to the Carrier to its respective addresses 
on file with the Commission. Attached was a copy of the notice of cancellation letter. 
The mailing was not returned to the Commission as undeliverable. 
5. The Commission did not receive a replacement Form E for the Carrier. On April 6, 2026, 
Ms. Burl issued a citation to the Carrier directing it to appear at a hearing on June 11, 
2026. Attached to the citation were the letters dated February 6, 2026, and March 13, 
2026. 
6. On April 7, 2026, Agent Hood mailed the citation via USPS regular mail and certified 
mail return receipt requested to the Carrier’s address on file with the Commission. 
Notice of the proceeding was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin on April 
10, 2026. 
7. When the matter was called on June 11, 2026, Midas Touch appeared and moved jointly 
with Commission Staff to continue the hearing to July 9, 2026. The motion was granted 
and the Ruling on Joint Motion to Continue and Notice of Rescheduled Hearing Date 
was issued that same day. 
8. The Carrier did not appear at the hearing on July 9, 2026. As of the hearing, the 
Commission had not received a replacement Form E, or any documents to close the 
Carrier’s LPSC account. 

Conclusions of Law 
1. At the hearing, the Commission Staff had the burden of proving its allegations against 
the Carrier. Because the Carrier did not appear, the Commission Staff also had the 
burden of demonstrating that the Carrier was provided fair notice of the hearing and the 
opportunity to present a defense. La. R.S. 45:166(A) provides that a certificate may be 
revoked “after notice and hearing for failure to comply with any provision of R.S. 
45:161 through 45:172, or with any lawful order, rule or regulation of the [C]ommission 
. . . .” 

2. Pursuant to its constitutional and statutory authority, the Commission adopted the Rules 
of Practice and Procedure. Commission Rules 7 and 19 provide for notice of non-
criminal proceedings through publication in the Commission’s Official Bulletin, as well 
as by service “through any means whereby proof of receipt or unclaimed status can be 
shown” to “the last known place of address of the person entitled to receive such notice 
. . . .”14 
3. Pursuant to constitutional and legislative mandate, and Commission orders adopted 
pursuant thereto, the Commission has the authority to regulate motor carriers and to 
ensure that they maintain levels of insurance required by statute and by Commission 
General Orders. The 2023 General Order provides that liability insurance shall be made 

14 Special Order Number 72-2021 dated November 22, 2001, Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte, In re: 
Possible implementation of Interim Rule 7 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure (Service of Process) 
and possible revision to the Commission’s Rules. 
Order No. T-37885 
Page 6 
on a Form E. La. R.S. 45:166(A) states the Commission may revoke a carrier’s authority 
for failure to comply with Commission rules. 
4. The Commission Staff demonstrated through testimonial and documentary evidence 
that the Carrier received notice of the hearing and Commission Staff’s allegations, 
chiefly the Ruling on Joint Motion to Continue and Notice of Rescheduled Date noting 
the appearance by Midas Touch when the matter was called on June 11, 2026, and its 
joint motion with Commission Staff to continue the hearing to July 9, 2026. Thus, the 
Carrier had the opportunity to appear and present a defense. 
5. The Commission Staff proved that the Carrier failed to provide a Form E indicating that 
its BI & PD liability insurance coverage had been extended beyond the February 3, 2026 
cancellation date stated in the Form K. 
6. We find that the Carrier failed to maintain the required proof of insurance coverage 
filing (a Form E) on file with the Commission as required by the 2023 General Order. 
Accordingly, we find that the Carrier is guilty of violating the 2023 General Order. 
7. We conclude that the Carrier’s failure to maintain proof of effective insurance coverage 
through a Form E constitutes a failure to comply with applicable law and Commission 
orders. Therefore, cancellation of the Carrier’s Common Carrier Certificates is 
warranted pursuant to La. R.S. 45:166(A). 
8. The 2006 General Order allows for the imposition of a $25 fee for the issuance of a 
citation by the Commission. Therefore, it is appropriate to require the Carrier to pay the 
$25 citation fee. 
Conclusion 

In accordance with the findings of fact and conclusions of law stated above: 
IT IS ORDERED that Common Carrier Certificate No. 7507-A, currently issued to DTK 
Enterprises, LLC dba Midas Touch Towing, is CANCELED due to the failure of DTK Enterprises, 
LLC dba Midas Touch Towing to maintain proof of insurance coverage on file with the 
Commission. 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that DTK Enterprises, LLC dba Midas Touch Towing pay 
a $25 citation fee to the Commission. 
BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA 
July 13, 2026
